author.name: Jannik Aßfalg
credits: repeat98: original 808/909 fixed-point engines and machine integration

presentation.summary: Play an original 808 or 909 bass drum as a track machine, with both effect slots available.
presentation.overview: Analog BD adds a track machine with two circuit-informed bass drum engines. Choose 808 or 909 from its engine browser and shape the sound on the SRC page. Synthesis runs before the stock AMP stage and both track effects. TDEP in the 909 and SAT in both engines now smooth modulation changes while preserving fixed-control sound.
highlights: Independent patches on all eight tracks
Both track effect slots remain available
usage: Assign ANALOG BD in the track machine chooser or SRC SETUP. Double-tap the track to open its engine browser; choose 808 or 909 with UP/DOWN or LEVEL and confirm with YES.
Shape the drum on SRC. The 808 has TONE and SWEEP; the 909 has TUNE and TDEP. Set accent, LPF and desk bands in SRC SETUP; AMP controls track volume.

Keep a separate project copy for stock firmware: saving an Analog BD project without this module can clamp its controls. Eight voices do not guarantee enough processing room for every effect combination.

controls.name: PITCH
controls.doc: 808 body pitch; 909 body frequency spans approximately 30–100 Hz.

controls.name: DECAY
controls.doc: Body decay, with a different response for each model.

controls.name: SWEEP / TDEP
controls.doc: 808 pitch excursion; 909 pitch-envelope amount with sample-wise smoothing.

controls.name: SAT
controls.doc: Drive into the shared Mackie desk stage, with smooth table interpolation during modulation.

controls.name: LPF
controls.doc: Output low-pass: OFF at 0, ORIG around 6.57 kHz at 64, 18 kHz at the assignment default 127.

limitations: SPRING REV is excluded from the upstream standalone remix; its shared DARK helper must be restored from local firmware.
Owner reports stable MKII 0.1.3 operation with distinct 808/909 instances and physical persistence. Maximum eight-voice FX load, worst-case chip timing and full memory bounds remain unqualified.
Saving this project on stock firmware can overwrite synth settings.

storage.label: DSP code
storage.conditions: Combined 808/909 glue and engines use 946 P words plus the separately preserved 35-word stock helper. Existing X allocation is unchanged; full lifetime/stack bounds remain unmeasured.

processing.label: DSP execution
processing.conditions: Peak executed instructions/sample in the focused modulation/retrigger workload; not worst-case chip cycles or full-chain utilization.

impact.conditions: Per active Analog BD voice with both models and rapid TDEP/SAT changes considered; unchanged ColdFire control path and existing shared DSP upload/table reservations. Ratings describe relative demand, not processor utilization or whole-chip headroom.

cpu.rationale: Existing guarded ColdFire machine/control glue publishes the same saved knob bytes; the smoothing runs entirely in DSP code and adds no ColdFire work.

dsp.rationale: Synthesis plus the desk stage and per-sample smoothing peaks at 268.375 executed instructions/sample for 808 and 386 for 909 in the focused workload, above the historical 220.9375/326.125 peaks. These are interpreter instruction counts, not chip timing.

memory.rationale: 946 P words per core and the separate 35-word helper reuse the existing donor. The 3776-word X upload per core includes tables and existing 64-word voice blocks; smoothing reuses scratch state and adds no X/Y/ColdFire allocation. Complete stack/lifetime bounds remain unmeasured.

tests.summary: TDEP/SAT smoothing passes constant-audio, modulation and native instance/core isolation tests. The owner reports stable MKII operation on the exact private build, with distinct 808/909 instances and settings/audio surviving Part/project reload and normal power-off/on. Emulator control-state persistence passes separately; worst-case chip timing, complete memory bounds and maximum FX load remain unmeasured.

tutorial.title: Smooth a long 909 tail
steps: In a disposable project, select the track, hold FUNC and press SRC for SRC SETUP, choose ANALOG BD and press YES. Double-tap its TRACK key, choose 909 with UP/DOWN or LEVEL and confirm with YES. Set LOW and HIGH to 64.

Press SRC to edit the main page. Set DECAY around 100, then trigger a hit and turn E (TDEP) and F (SAT) through the ranges that reproduced the report. Repeat with the existing modulation assignment. The update should reduce control steps while retaining the original endpoints and saturation character.

Set modulation depth to zero, return SAT to 0 and TDEP to 64, then press STOP and let the tail finish. Select 808 in the same browser to compare SAT; its knob values are retained when switching engines.

access.location: Audio track SRC SETUP: ANALOG BD; double-tap the track key for its 808 / 909 engine browser.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press SRC to open SRC SETUP. Use DOWN to reach ANALOG BD, then press YES to assign it.
Press SRC to close SETUP and edit the main controls. The 808 model uses PITCH, DECAY, TONE, ATK, SWEEP and SAT; the 909 uses TUNE and TDEP in place of TONE and SWEEP.
Double-tap the assigned track’s TRACK key to open the engine browser. Choose 808 or 909 with UP/DOWN or LEVEL, then press YES. Selecting a model retains the existing knob settings.
Hold FUNC and press SRC for the shared ACCNT, LPF, LOW and HIGH controls. AMP and the track FX pages remain available.
